Subtraction of the exact mean-background Moran value factors into positive denominators times d^2[(m-a)(m+2a)-d^2]. The three exhaustive a/m cases and sharp interior variance root follow by sign arithmetic. Independent seven-state rational transient-chain solves for seven rational triples and a symbolic factorization checker both run to VERIFY_OK; the general theorem is algebraic and does not infer infinity from finite samples.

originality.rationale: The complete three-individual discrete Moran averaging-bias sign diagram (including an interior fixed-mean variance crossover) is not stated or implied by the compared specific results. The closest directly matching multiallele Moran article Braga et al. proves only first-order weak-selection approximation, whereas the bias is at least third order near neutrality. Ferreira--Neves supply a general discrete harmonic system, not the exact signed comparison. The motivating 2026 study computes a Wright--Fisher diffusion/Kimura comparator rather than the exact Moran-vs-Moran difference. This is a scoped, self-review with documented literature risks, not an assertion of absolute worldwide uniqueness.
residual_risks: A generic discrete Moran transition-matrix method can reproduce N=3 fixation values; the genuinely specific novelty asserted is the full sharp comparison to mean-competitor fixation and fixed-mean variance sign reversal, not the Markov equations.
Unindexed or differently named small-population exact-calculation literature may contain an equivalent comparison.

value.rationale: Exact competitor aggregation is a natural model-reduction question raised by recent multi-allele fixation work. This classifies the entire positive-fitness domain for the smallest genuinely three-allele Moran population, not an arbitrary numerical slice. It distinguishes always-overestimated, always-underestimated and variance-dependent regimes, and shows a strict reversal at fixed target fitness and fixed background mean. The signed error appears beyond first order under weak selection, explaining why prior weak-selection formulas miss this effect. The N=3 boundary is a finite-population structural benchmark, without claiming large-N relevance.
